title: Thermospheric density response to the May 2024 Gannon geostorm: multi-perspective characterisation and operational impact on satellites
excerpt:
The May 2024 Gannon geomagnetic storm was one of the strongest of this solar cycle and the first of its magnitude to affect an environment with over 10,000 active satellites. Operators rely on different combinations of observations and models to characterise the storm-time thermosphere, and how widely these sources disagree under operational latency constraints (i.e., publication delay ≤ 24 h) is itself an operationally relevant quantity. We quantify this disagreement for the Gannon event across three measurement spaces: temperature, neutral density, and orbit.

In the temperature and neutral-density spaces we compare FPI temperatures and POD- and TLE-derived densities against two operational atmospheric models, NRLMSISE-00 (climatology) and WAM-IPE (first-principles). In orbit space we examine TLE-SGP4 prediction error, catalogue-wide decay, and the non-conservative force balance.

At ∼250 km altitude, ground-based Fabry–Perot Interferometer (FPI) measurements at Millstone Hill and Cachoeira Paulista showed 40%–65% storm-time temperature increases; both NRLMSISE-00 and WAM-IPE, run in nowcast and 48-h forecast configurations, reproduced less than half of this response, with the gap largest under forecast drivers. title: Embodied mindfulness for sleep disturbance in psychotherapy: extending metacognitive models through sensorimotor regulation
excerpt:
Insomnia is increasingly understood as a disorder of insufficient de-arousal involving interacting cognitive-emotional and physiological processes. Mindfulness-based approaches may reduce insomnia by modifying attentional and metacognitive responses to wakefulness; however, prevailing theoretical accounts and therapeutic practices have predominantly examined mindfulness in formats involving relatively little overt movement, leaving the specific regulatory contributions of sustained movement–breath coordination and dynamically changing sensorimotor feedback comparatively underdeveloped.

This hypothesis and theory paper proposes an Embodied Mindfulness Framework that extends established metacognitive accounts of insomnia by conceptualizing mindfulness as a dynamic brain–body process. Embodied mindfulness is defined as present-centered, nonjudgmental awareness cultivated through coordinated attention, breathing, posture, bodily sensation, and intentional movement, with Tai Chi presented as a representative therapeutic format.

The framework proposes bodily awareness, intentional movement, and sensorimotor integration as interdependent processes through which embodied regulation is cultivated. At the mechanistic level, we hypothesize that autonomic flexibility, interoceptive reappraisal, and attentional anchoring operate reciprocally to alter how cognitive, emotional, and physiological activation is experienced and regulated…

title: The PAL framework as a recursive model of consciousness transformation in contemplative practice
excerpt:
Meditation research explains a good deal about what practice does to attention and emotion. It explains much less about how years of practice change the structure of conscious experience and the sense of self. This article presents the Prerequisites–Aspects–Levels (PAL) framework as a recursive model of that change. PAL comes from a published grounded theory study of 27 long-term practitioners of Integrated Amrita Meditation®-35 (IAM®-35). We keep the original categories and add a theoretical reading.

Motivational-affective conditions, process-level dynamics and transformations of experience are proposed to act on one another in both directions over time. We define six candidate directed links among the three domains, separate passing states from lasting change, and show where PAL’s predictions part from those of the self-awareness, self-regulation and self-transcendence model, predictive-processing accounts, the Topographic Reorganisation Model and spiral models. Five propositions state the measures, the expected order of events and the results that would count against the framework.

Neural correlates are offered as candidates for testing and not as support. PAL rests on one practice, one dataset and retrospective reports, and we say what that limits. We offer PAL as a testable model that should be revised or abandoned if the tests go against it.

title: Aperiodic EEG–pupil coupling during naturalistic video viewing in children and adolescents
excerpt:
IntroductionMultimodal physiological approaches can characterize complementary aspects of emotional processing that are not available from a single signal.MethodsWe analyzed synchronized high-density EEG and eye-tracking recordings from a publicly available developmental dataset of children and adolescents younger than 18 years who viewed negative, neutral, and positive naturalistic videos.

The SPRiNT algorithm provided time-resolved aperiodic EEG Exponent and Offset estimates, and their dependence with pupil diameter was quantified using mutual information (MI) and correlation-based coupling metrics within labeled scalp sensor groups.ResultsIn the original analysis, Friedman tests showed a consistent condition effect for both Offset-pupil and Exponent-pupil MI across all six scalp groups (Kendall's W = 0.762 − 0.830, all pFDR<10-7).

Pairwise tests showed greater MI during the negative video than during the neutral or positive videos (standardized r = 0.869 − 0.874, all pFDR<10-7), whereas no neutral-positive MI difference was detected.DiscussionBy integrating cortical spectral dynamics with a peripheral measure of arousal and attention, this approach provides a framework for studying brain-autonomic coordination during naturalistic emotional processing in children and adolescents.

title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
excerpt:
Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.

Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.

But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next…

excerpt:

Did you come across as annoying? Did you say something weird? Mostly, it’s easy to assume the person on the other end saw your message, shrugged, and didn’t think twice about ignoring you.

We tend to picture ghosting as a cold, deliberate brush-off. In everyday digital life, though, silence is often far messier: someone glances at a text while distracted, means to answer later, and forgets, or puts off replying without realizing the other person already feels shut out…
